clue.text: Important little woman's crime

parts.note: important means big, as in a big decision
Amy March is one of the sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women

explanation.surface: Some significant small lady has committed an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little woman' reads as a small lady, but it points to one of the four March sisters in Little Women, Amy; the possessive 's just links her to the crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying while already legally married to someone else is a criminal offence in many countries.

clue.text: Flaw on outside of space vehicle is mistake

indicators.note: on outside of places the word for mistake around the vehicle

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder
LEM is the Lunar Excursion Module of the Apollo missions

explanation.surface: A defect on the exterior of a spacecraft is an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on outside of' puts BISH, which is informal British slang for a blunder, around the Apollo lunar module.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish is a mark or defect spoiling the appearance of something, a fault.

clue.text: Mushroom that's left below bark

indicators.note: below places the abbreviation for left beneath the verb in this down clue

parts.note: to mushroom is to grow rapidly

explanation.surface: A fungus left underneath tree bark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mushroom' and 'bark' paint a woodland picture, but mushroom is a verb meaning grow and bark is a dog's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A growl is a low threatening sound a dog makes, like a bark.

clue.text: This person given exceptional award, a Nobel prizewinner

parts.note: this person refers to the setter, me

indicators.note: exceptional means out of the ordinary, so the letters of award are rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter receives an extraordinary honour, becoming a Nobel laureate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person' is the setter speaking of himself, a common crossword device; 'exceptional' rearranges the letters of award.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Medawar shared the 1960 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for work on immunological tolerance.

clue.text: Constitutional rights finally being acknowledged in Scandinavia

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word rights

parts.note: a troll is a creature of Scandinavian folklore, a being whose existence is acknowledged there

explanation.surface: Civil liberties at last gaining recognition in the Nordic countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constitutional' looks like part of the political picture, but here it is a noun: a walk taken for one's health.
explanation.definitionFit: A constitutional is a gentle walk taken for health, the same as a leisurely amble.

clue.text: Everton strict ultimately in relation to payments

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word strict

parts.note: of can mean concerning or about, as in to speak of
fees are payments for services

explanation.surface: The football club is rigorous, at the end of the day, about money.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Liverpool football club nicknamed the Toffees, after a local sweet shop; Everton toffee is also a sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton Football Club's long-standing nickname comes from toffee once made and sold near its ground.

clue.text: Moving into gear, I start

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Shifting into gear, I set off in my car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges the letters of INTO GEAR plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin or come into being, the verb sense of start.

clue.text: No joke for someone on the rack!

definitions.text: No joke for someone on the rack!

parts.words: No joke for someone on the rack!
parts.note: a teasing hoax described as literal torture, since the rack stretched a victim's limbs

explanation.definitionFit: A leg-pull is a practical joke or tease, and on the rack a leg literally gets pulled.

clue.text: Peril that besets soldiers

indicators.note: besets means surrounds, so the word that encloses the soldiers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A danger that surrounds troops.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a stock crossword abbreviation for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is a source of danger, so it serves as a synonym for peril.

clue.text: One frightened by outlandish sixties' show

indicators.note: outlandish means bizarre or strange, so the letters of the preceding words are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: Someone scared by a weird revue from the 1960s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlandish' rearranges the fifteen letters of ONE FRIGHTENED BY.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous satirical stage revue starring Peter Cook, Dudley Moore, Alan Bennett and Jonathan Miller opened in 1960.

clue.text: Weeping one? Gosh, sick inside!

indicators.note: inside places the word for sick within the exclamation

parts.note: gosh and wow are both exclamations of surprise
sick means ill

explanation.surface: Someone crying exclaims in surprise that they feel nauseous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weeping one' sounds like a crying person, but it is a tree: the weeping willow.
explanation.definitionFit: The weeping willow is a tree whose drooping branches give it that name.

clue.text: See 23
The commander, despicable person who claims divine authority?

parts.note: taken as written
OC is the military abbreviation for Officer Commanding
a rat is a contemptible or treacherous person

explanation.surface: A military leader turns out to be a scoundrel who believes he rules by God's will.
explanation.definitionFit: A theocrat governs, or seeks to govern, in the name of God, claiming religious authority for their power.

clue.text: Proceeding correctly, like a gymnast?

definitions.meaning: an idiom meaning on the right track
a gymnast performs balanced on a narrow wooden apparatus

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means on the right track, and literally describes a gymnast balanced on the apparatus.

clue.text: Bit of wire in bread?

definitions.meaning: a small bent piece of wire used to fasten papers together
bread is a basic food, a principal item in the diet

explanation.definitionFit: A staple is both a small U-shaped fastener of wire and a basic foodstuff such as bread.

clue.text: Fly with jet set separately

indicators.note: with signals that the answer is held within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Travelling by air with the glamorous international set, but each on their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' signals letters held in the run of words: jeT SET SEparately.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is a biting African fly that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Extend jaunt away from home

parts.note: a spin is a short drive or ride for pleasure
out means not at home

explanation.surface: Lengthen a pleasure trip away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extend' is the definition, a verb: to make something last longer.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin something out is to prolong it, making it last longer than needed.

clue.text: Enthusiast for conservation? One adapts to the environment

definitions.meaning: a green-minded sort of person, a lover of ecology
a biological term for a population adapted to local conditions

explanation.definitionFit: In biology an ecotype is a distinct population adapted to its habitat; jokingly, a green type of person.

clue.text: Composer adding sort of stroke to score

parts.note: a masse is a billiards or snooker shot played with the cue held nearly upright
to net means to score or gain, as in netting a profit

explanation.surface: A songwriter incorporating a kind of musical stroke into a score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stroke' and 'score' suggest music or sport generally; the stroke is a masse shot in billiards.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Massenet was a French composer of operas such as Manon and Werther.

clue.text: Change in ministry problematical — half the females unwanted

parts.note: MOD is the Ministry of Defence

indicators.note: unwanted means the halved females are thrown out of the word for problematical

parts.note: iffy means doubtful or problematic

indicators.note: half the takes one of the pair of letters standing for females

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female, so two of them are FF

explanation.surface: A rethink in government, troublesome as half the women are not wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: MOD is Britain's Ministry of Defence; 'half the females unwanted' drops one of the two Fs from IFFY, leaving IFY.
explanation.definitionFit: To modify is to alter, the verb sense of change.

clue.text: What the married woman may change certainly holds fellow up

definitions.text: What the married woman may change

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the word for certainly holds the reversed fellow

parts.note: sure means certainly, as in sure, I'll help

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A bride's adoption of a new name certainly holds a man up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the man round because this is a down clue, and 'holds' puts the result inside the word for certainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditionally a woman may take her husband's family name on marriage.

clue.text: Around end of summer save a bit

indicators.note: around means the word for save goes round the final letter

parts.note: save means except, as in all save one

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of summer

explanation.surface: At the close of summer, keep a little money aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' looks like a verb, but it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a short extract from a longer work, a bit taken out of it.

clue.text: Door wife chopped up into sticks for burning?

indicators.note: chopped up means cut into pieces, so the letters of the words before it are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A door and a wife hacked to pieces to be put on the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped up' rearranges the letters of DOOR WIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: Logs and kindling cut for a fire are sticks intended to be burnt.

clue.text: Artistic style of clown getting nothing right in turn at first

indicators.note: at first places the reversed pair at the start, ahead of the clown
in turn means turned round, so the zero and the letter for right are read backwards

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
Coco the Clown was a famous circus clown

explanation.surface: A clown's art movement gets nowhere because of correctness at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' turns O and R round to give RO, and 'at first' puts that before COCO; Coco the Clown was a celebrated British circus performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is an ornate eighteenth-century decorative style in art and architecture.

clue.text: Is individual able to earn American title given to retired cleric?

parts.note: able to means can
an individual is one
to earn something is to merit it
US is the abbreviation for American, as in the United States

explanation.surface: Can one person deserve an American honorific when a clergyman retires?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks a question; the clue reads 'Is individual able' as 'can one', then MERIT and US.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus is an honorary title for one retired from office, and a canon is a cathedral clergyman.

clue.text: Yes-man conformed, looking ridiculous in satirical presentation

indicators.note: looking ridiculous suggests something absurdly distorted, so the preceding letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sycophant fell into line and appeared absurd in a send-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking ridiculous' rearranges the fifteen letters of YES-MAN CONFORMED.
explanation.definitionFit: This genre of play satirises the behaviour and pretensions of fashionable society, as in Wilde or Congreve.

clue.text: Cool cushion

definitions.meaning: to cool, as in quenching hot metal to harden it
to soften or moderate an effect, as in to soften a blow

explanation.definitionFit: To temper steel involves cooling it, and to temper criticism is to soften or moderate it.

clue.text: Note about cheese-maker's requirement

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for the banknote is read backwards

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote in Britain

explanation.surface: A memo concerning what someone making cheese needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests a memo or musical note, but it is a banknote: a TENNER is British slang for a ten-pound note, and 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rennet is the enzyme preparation used to curdle milk when making cheese.
